labels.label: T-abs-one-sided-future-base/future-base
findings: Library, not paper. No existing statement wrote C.dual.ChronalPastNeighbours or C.dual.NoPastEndpoint (grep of Causal/ and scaffold/), so after the swap no statement reads as a double dual. Every use of the old future side was the projection h.2 or the term-mode argument (C := C.dual) h.2, and these still elaborate: C.ChronalFutureNeighbours and C.dual.ChronalPastNeighbours are definitionally equal by one delta step and structure eta (C.dual.dual is C by rfl, Causality.dual_dual).
questions: Reading taken (the dispatch allowed either): ChronalNeighbours is re-expressed as C.ChronalPastNeighbours ∧ C.ChronalFutureNeighbours. The alternative was to keep the text C.ChronalPastNeighbours ∧ C.dual.ChronalPastNeighbours, whose second conjunct would then unfold to C.dual.dual.ChronalFutureNeighbours. I kept the order, past first (.1) and future second (.2), so every projection keeps its meaning and every conjunct is definitionally what it was (probe.lean: Iff.rfl against the old body and against Lemma K's hZm ∧ hZp). The same holds for NoCausalEndpoint := C.NoPastEndpoint ∧ C.NoFutureEndpoint. The alternative ordering, the future first as CausallyOpen and LocallyCausallyOpen have it, would have swapped .1 and .2 for every user, so I did not take it.

Names chosen after CausallyOpenFuture: ChronalFutureNeighbours and NoFutureEndpoint (the dispatch's examples). Bridge names: chronalPastNeighbours_def and noPastEndpoint_def (the old bodies, Iff.rfl). These follow mathlib's _def for an unfolding, because noPastEndpoint_iff was already taken by the characterisation ∃ y ≠ x, y ≤ x. The others are dual_chronalFutureNeighbours, dual_chronalPastNeighbours, dual_noFutureEndpoint and dual_noPastEndpoint (kb/0002), and chronalNeighbours_iff_future and noCausalEndpoint_iff_future (each two-sided notion as the future base of C.dual and of C).

redefined_keeping_name_and_statement.Causal.Causality.NoPastEndpoint: Causal/LadderLocal.lean:188 (HEAD :168). Now C.dual.NoFutureEndpoint. Before: ∀ x, C.Jminus ⊤ {x} ≠ {x}. Equal by Iff.rfl (noPastEndpoint_def).
redefined_keeping_name_and_statement.Causal.Causality.ChronalNeighbours: Causal/LadderLocal.lean:178 (HEAD :164). Now C.ChronalPastNeighbours ∧ C.ChronalFutureNeighbours. extra_decls: Causal.Causality.noFutureEndpoint_iff (LadderLocal :433): C.NoFutureEndpoint ↔ ∀ x, ∃ y, y ≠ x ∧ C.le ⊤ x y. Proved directly: it is HEAD's proof of noPastEndpoint_iff with Jminus replaced by Jplus. noPastEndpoint_iff is now its C.dual (kb/0002).
Causal.Causality.ChronalFutureNeighbours.mem_Zplus (LadderLocal :358): with future neighbours every point is in Z⁺. This is ChronalPastNeighbours.mem_Zminus for C.dual.

Causal.Causality.AbsolutelyMinimal.chronalFutureNeighbours_iff (LadderLocal :387): on a T1 space with absolute minimality, ChronalFutureNeighbours ↔ ∀ x, (C.Iplus ⊤ {x}).Nonempty. This is the past form for C.dual.

Causal.IsCausalIso.chronalFutureNeighbours_iff, Causal.IsCausalIso.noFutureEndpoint_iff (CausalIsoInvariance :744, :759): invariance of the two new bases. Each is h.dual.…Past…_iff. They keep the module's claim that every side condition of Causal.LadderLocal is invariant.

downstream_proofs_changed.why: HEAD's `rw [Precausality.mem_Jminus_singleton]` no longer finds Jminus, because the goal now shows C.dual.Jplus. The proof is moved verbatim, with Jminus replaced by Jplus, to the new noFutureEndpoint_iff (:433). noPastEndpoint_iff becomes `noFutureEndpoint_iff (C := C.dual)`. Its statement is unchanged.

The future conjunct was `Causality.noPastEndpoint_iff.2 …`, which the unifier had read as C.dual's. The expected type is now lightlikeLine.NoFutureEndpoint, and NoPastEndpoint ?C cannot be unified with it, so the conjunct now calls `Causality.noFutureEndpoint_iff.2 …`. The witness term is the same (show p ≤ p + 1 ∧ _). One line changed.

After `rw [ChronalNeighbours]` the future side is C.ChronalFutureNeighbours, so `rw [AbsolutelyMinimal.chronalPastNeighbours_iff hd]` (hd for C.dual) finds no occurrence. It now rewrites with AbsolutelyMinimal.chronalFutureNeighbours_iff h, and the now unused `have hd` is removed. Two lines changed.
The same, with the new CausallyArcConnected.chronalFutureNeighbours_iff hC (:236). `have hd` removed.

downstream_proofs_unchanged_note: No other proof was touched. Every other user compiles as it was: the 11 uses in ChronalNeighbourBridge apart from the two above, CausalIsoInvariance (chronalPastNeighbours, chronalNeighbours_iff, noPastEndpoint_iff and noCausalEndpoint_iff, all unchanged), SingularCauchy (hJ x), NotchedPlane (intro V v hv; exact ⟨p, hp, TransGen.single hst⟩), Ladder/Dual and Rules/Test/DualTest, and the 17 other modules whose source names ChronalNeighbours or NoCausalEndpoint. 42 of their proof terms change hash anyway, with unchanged source (dump-diff.txt (d)). Each term embeds the new unfolding (C.dual.lt V v p where it had C.lt V p v), which is definitionally the same.

chronal_neighbours_check: ChronalNeighbours still means the conjunction of both sides, the past side first. Its body is C.ChronalPastNeighbours ∧ C.ChronalFutureNeighbours, the past as the future base of C.dual (chronalNeighbours_iff_future, Iff.rfl). probe.lean checks by Iff.rfl that it is the old C.ChronalPastNeighbours ∧ C.dual.ChronalPastNeighbours and Lemma K's hZm ∧ hZp. It checks by projection that h.2 : C.dual.ChronalPastNeighbours still typechecks, that ⟨h, h'⟩ with h' : C.dual.ChronalPastNeighbours still builds it, and that causallyOpen_of_pushUp hp h.1 h.2 (Causal.LemmaK) applies. The ladder tactic's rules name it only as a head constant (Rules.lean:62, 64, 66; Dual.lean:239-243), and DualTest (1626 lines) and Test compile unchanged. NoCausalEndpoint passes the same checks.

kb_proposals: The one-sided chronal and endpoint notions have the future as base (DEC-166 (a), T-abs-one-sided-future-base). Causality.ChronalFutureNeighbours (∀ V, ∀ v ∈ V, ∃ p ∈ V, v ≪_V p) and NoFutureEndpoint (J⁺(x) ≠ {x}) are the definitions. ChronalPastNeighbours := C.dual.ChronalFutureNeighbours and NoPastEndpoint := C.dual.NoFutureEndpoint; their old bodies are chronalPastNeighbours_def and noPastEndpoint_def, by Iff.rfl. ChronalNeighbours := C.ChronalPastNeighbours ∧ C.ChronalFutureNeighbours and NoCausalEndpoint := C.NoPastEndpoint ∧ C.NoFutureEndpoint, with .1 past and .2 future as before. The duals dual_chronalFutureNeighbours/PastNeighbours and dual_noFutureEndpoint/PastEndpoint are Iff.rfl, and each one-sided lemma has its future form (noFutureEndpoint_iff, ChronalFutureNeighbours.mem_Zplus, .Iplus_nonempty(_of_mem), AbsolutelyMinimal/CausallyArcConnected.chronalFutureNeighbours_iff, IsCausalIso.chronalFutureNeighbours_iff, .noFutureEndpoint_iff). Update kb/0053, which says 'past form ChronalPastNeighbours'.

Pitfall after the swap: `rw [ChronalNeighbours, foo_iff (C := C.dual) …]` no longer finds C.dual.ChronalPastNeighbours, because the future side is now syntactically C.ChronalFutureNeighbours. Rewrite with the future-form lemma, or with `← dual_chronalPastNeighbours`. Term-mode `h.2` passed where C.dual.ChronalPastNeighbours is expected still elaborates: C.dual.dual is C by structure eta, Causality.dual_dual is rfl.

A definition-body refactor that keeps every statement has a different check from a verbatim hoist (kb/0063). Check the statements by `#check @n` byte-identity on every declaration that mentions the notions. Expect value-hash changes in proofs whose source is unchanged, since elaborated terms embed the unfolded types, and type changes in the definition's eq_1 and in term-mode matchers (kb/0066). These are not regressions. List them by class, and verify 'source unchanged' block by block against `git archive HEAD`.

Pitfall: `python3 tools/ladder.py emit-lean --help` RUNS emit-lean. The tool ignores extra arguments and writes Causal/Ladder/Rules.lean and Test.lean in place. For a dry run, call ladder.emit_lean / ladder.emit_test in memory (campaign/T-abs-one-sided-future-base/emit_probe.py). DualTest's generator takes an output path: `dual_closure.py shipped /tmp/x.lean`.

notes: Exclusive strict-library refactor, with no statement changed and no declaration removed or renamed. Four definitions got new bodies, with names and types kept, 18 declarations were added, and 4 proofs changed (listed above). For the master: (1) Docstrings were updated in the four edited files: LadderLocal (the module bullets for chronal-neighbours and no-causal-endpoint, the first SCOPE bullet, now 'The future is the base …', and the six definitions' docstrings), ChronalNeighbourBridge (bullets 0 and 1, plus two stale line references: LadderLocal.lean:163 -> :178 and :93–94 -> :100–101, which were already one line off at HEAD), CausalIsoInvariance (the ladder bullet lists the two new invariance lemmas) and Ladder/Dual (the 'No rule is given for …' bullet no longer says DEC-166 will rename; it names the future bases). (2) Outside my write set, now stale or worth refreshing: kb/entries/0053 ('past form ChronalPastNeighbours'); README.md's rows for Causal.LadderLocal (:61) and Causal.ChronalNeighbourBridge (:69), which list the named side conditions without the two future bases; programme/ladder.toml (see notes_for_keeper); the generated reports/atlas and reports/blueprint, which cite CausalIsoInvariance and LadderLocal line numbers (CausalIsoInvariance: +1 after :38, +5 after :743, +9 after :758). (3) papers/ers-predictability lists Causal/LadderLocal.lean in ersthm:ThmNotBlocking's lean_files. Its decls do not change, but ers_theorem_4_82_of_oneSidedBoundary moved :399 -> :478, so regenerate if the ledger records lines. (4) Optional follow-up, not done because those proofs compile unchanged: ChronalNeighbours.mem_Zplus, ChronalNeighbours.Iplus_nonempty and similar users pass h.2 to a past lemma at C.dual, and could cite the new future forms (h.2.mem_Zplus, h.2.Iplus_nonempty).
